html:
The Nyulnyul are an Aboriginal Australian people of the Dampier Peninsula in the Kimberley of Western Australia, around Beagle Bay. The map shows them as Nyul Nyul from 1600 to 1815. Their language gave its name to the Nyulnyulan family of languages of the region; it is no longer spoken as a first language.

Their neighbours were the Jabirr Jabirr to the south, the Nimanburu and Ngumbarl to the southeast and the Bardi to the north. In 1890 French Trappist monks founded a Catholic mission at Beagle Bay, later run by German Pallottine priests. Its church, built by the community in 1918, is famous for an altar decorated with pearl shell. Many children taken from their families elsewhere were also sent to the mission.
